identity_evidence.quote: A 18-year old first Gravida at 31 weeks of gestation developed a severe sepsis caused by an obstructive pyelonephritis.

attribution_limitations: The abstract places the caesarean section at 33 weeks of gestation while the case description gives 32 weeks and 2 days. Two different numbers for one value: both sides are review-only and the delivery gestational age is not used elsewhere.

The abstract describes the rupture at a gestational age of 31 weeks, whereas the case description gives 31 weeks of gestation at the onset of sepsis and the suspected rupture four days after opioid induction. The abstract wording is not used as a fact.

The text and Figure 1 caption give the enlarged fetal bladder as 47 × 40 mm; the caliper readout printed inside the Figure 1 image shows a single different length. Image-printed values are pixel content, not a fact or conflict side; the diameter fact is review-only while the enlarged-bladder finding stays included.

Hematoma certainty differs by caption: Figure 2 caption names a prevesical hematoma, Figure 3 caption names a suspected prevesical hematoma. The text states hematoma without qualifier. No resolution is inferred.
The creatinine unit is printed "ymol/L" (probably a print artefact for a micromole unit); kept literal and no unit conversion or correction is applied.

The authors call the case opioid treatment related, but the abstract and discussion state there is no clear proof of a connection between maternal opioid treatment and fetal bladder rupture. Causation is not asserted as a fact.
The "Concord Birth Trolley" was an initial aim before the placenta detached; the source does not say whether it was used, so no device fact is recorded.

The mother is the index patient; the fetus and newborn have their own course (fetal bladder rupture, neonatal drainage and surgery) but are presented within one case, so they stay in this record with subject fetus or newborn (ROSTER-RELATIVES), as in the corpus precedent of a mother-index record holding the newborn's own workup and intensive care.

The Figure 2 image prints a caliper length that rounds to the 28 mm stated in the caption (rounding difference); the caption value is kept and the image value stays pixel content in the visual review.
The Figure 3 caption names a fetal bladder rupture without hedging, while the case text says a possible spontaneous bladder rupture was suspected; the rupture is kept as possible.

The Figure 5 caption describes a dorsal wall defect at the 4th postpartal hour, while the text sentence citing Figure 5 says a dorsolateral defect was confirmed by ultrasound without a time; the caption time is not transferred to the text diagnosis.

The six-day sedation course and the two- and four-day ultrasound findings are anchored to the introduction of opioid treatment; the relations order the start of the drug course before those findings, not its end.
